mechanism: The claim is recognized as second-order (for example acceleration).
orderedRateSeries(evidence) does not produce two safely comparable explicit rates.
The runtime falls back to generic evidence quantities via evidenceQuantities.map(scaled).
Absolute financial levels, isolated rates, and other numbers can therefore be treated as if they were a comparable rate series.
A directional SUPPORTS or COUNTERS result is emitted instead of fail-closed abstention.
families.safetyInvariantViolated: Second-order direction must never be inferred from generic numeric quantities when an explicit comparable rate series is unavailable.

boundary: Remove generic-quantity fallback from second-order resolution.
Resolve second-order direction only from explicitly recognized comparable rates with temporal binding.
If fewer than two comparable rates are available, return ABSTAINED + AMBIGUOUS.
Do not attempt to improve total benchmark accuracy in the same repair.

mechanism: The claim and evidence both contain causal language and overlapping financial concepts.
causalDecision can return SUPPORTS before explicit outcome direction is checked.
The evidence states that operating profit decreased and that higher volume only partially offset negative drivers.
The claim states that higher volume fully offset the pressure and caused operating profit to increase.
The causal-support path therefore outranks explicit contradictory outcome evidence.
families.safetyInvariantViolated: An explicit contradiction in the claimed outcome must veto a SUPPORTS decision from causal-attribution heuristics.

boundary: Check explicit claimed-outcome direction against evidence before emitting causal SUPPORTS.
A clear outcome contradiction must return COUNTERS or safely abstain; it must never return SUPPORTS.
Preserve causal role alignment for non-contradictory cases.
Treat fully-offset versus partially-offset wording as an additional contradiction signal only when safely bound.

repairPriority.rationale: This single unsafe fallback explains four of the five archived safety failures and can be repaired conservatively by removing a directional fallback rather than adding semantic coverage.
This addresses the most severe single inversion, COUNTERS→SUPPORTS, but is isolated after the broader second-order safety defect.

nonGoals: Do not repair general causal-attribution recall.
Do not repair mix inference, scope binding, or ordinary hard negatives.
Do not change v0.2C gold labels, gate thresholds, dataset bytes, or first-blind result.
Do not promote R2 to the default runtime.
Do not optimize overall accuracy during the safety-repair phase.
